subject.title: fix(process): bound Windows exec timeout cleanup

question: Should Windows foreground exec settlement remain bounded when taskkill exceeds the three-second completion limit, accepting that descendant termination is not confirmed in that exceptional path?
rationale: The patch is correct and strongly proven for normal and observed failure paths, but choosing bounded caller availability over guaranteed descendant cleanup when taskkill itself hangs is intentional runtime policy.

options.title: Accept bounded settlement
options.body: Merge the current design so foreground exec cannot wait indefinitely when Windows taskkill itself stalls.

options.title: Require confirmed cleanup
options.body: Pause and redesign the contract if every descendant must be confirmed terminated before foreground exec may settle.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded settlement
recommendation.body: Merge the current design so foreground exec cannot wait indefinitely when Windows taskkill itself stalls.
